epistemic_codes.H: Historically / textually attested (present in the primary source itself)
epistemic_codes.D: Original Didacus artistic invention or interpretation

meta.confidence_scale_note: evidence_confidence labels (High/Moderate/Low) are quoted or closely paraphrased from the source paper. The numeric encoding used for charts (High=3, Moderate=2, Low=1) is a derived scoring convention created for this analysis, not a value stated in the source.

archangels.name: Michael
archangels.historical_role: Chief/great prince associated with protection of Daniel's people; placed in an eschatological setting of crisis and deliverance; called 'the archangel' disputing with the devil; fights the dragon; one of the seven holy angels in 1 Enoch 20, assigned to the best part of humankind and to chaos.

attributes.name: Armour
attributes.note: development of visual tradition, not a literal description in Daniel or 1 Enoch

attributes.name: Sword
attributes.note: represents decisive boundary-setting in Didacus reading

attributes.name: Shield
attributes.note: clearest visual carrier of 'protection' in the Didacus redesign

attributes.name: Defeated dragon
attributes.note: developed from Revelation 12 narrative into a static attribute

archangels.methodological_caution: Avoid saying that the sword or shield is explicitly prescribed by Daniel or 1 Enoch. Avoid claiming that viewing the image activates a specific 'protection circuit.'
contemplative_prompts: What deserves protection?
What boundary requires courage?
Where is decisive action necessary?

archangels.name: Gabriel
archangels.historical_role: Helps Daniel understand a vision, arriving in 'swift flight'; appears in Luke's annunciation narratives announcing major births; in 1 Enoch 20 assigned to Paradise, the serpents, and the cherubim.

attributes.name: White lily
attributes.note: strongly established in Western Annunciation imagery, later medieval/Renaissance

attributes.name: Scroll
attributes.note: Didacus addition referencing authority, message and interpretation together

attributes.name: Flowing wings
attributes.note: used to distinguish Gabriel's geometry from Michael's harder axial form

archangels.methodological_caution: Do not state that Gabriel is historically defined by the lily in every tradition. 'Silence' is a Didacus poetic interpretation, not a primary-source title.
contemplative_prompts: What message is waiting to be received or given?
What needs to be spoken plainly?
What is the difference between information and revelation?

archangels.name: Raphael
archangels.historical_role: Accompanies Tobias and assists with restoring Tobit's sight in the Book of Tobit; identifies himself as one of the seven holy angels who stand before God; in 1 Enoch 20 assigned to the spirits of human beings.

attributes.name: Fish
attributes.note: directly rooted in Tobit's narrative — the fish's organs are part of the healing events

attributes.name: Caduceus / medical symbolism
attributes.note: explicitly flagged in the paper as NOT an ancient Raphael-specific attribute; earlier manuscript claim should be corrected

attributes.name: Vertical star sequence (anatomical metaphor)
attributes.note: explicitly an original Didacus device, not a traditional Raphael symbol

archangels.methodological_caution: The manuscript's earlier caduceus statement should be removed or rewritten; the caduceus is not a historically specific Raphael attribute.
contemplative_prompts: What in life needs repair?
Where has balance been lost?
What active practice would restoration require?

archangels.name: Uriel
archangels.historical_role: One of the seven named angels in 1 Enoch 20, assigned over the world and Tartarus; becomes associated with knowledge and interpretation in later Jewish and Christian reception; outside the usual three archangels named in most Western biblical canons.

attributes.name: Book
attributes.note: later art/esoteric/devotional tradition; not one universally authoritative costume

attributes.name: Open book (as used)
attributes.note: Didacus semantic bridge from later knowledge traditions to the illumination theme

attributes.name: Globe/fire geometry
attributes.note: references 1 Enoch jurisdiction over the world and Tartarus

archangels.methodological_caution: Do not present the burning book or a flame-tipped staff as historically prescribed attributes of Uriel; they are contemporary iconographic synthesis.
contemplative_prompts: What have I not allowed myself to understand?
Where do I prefer comfort to clarity?
What changes when understanding becomes action?

archangels.name: Raguel
archangels.historical_role: One of the seven angels in 1 Enoch 20, assigned to the world of the luminaries with a jurisdiction involving vengeance or judgement — an astronomical and judicial role rather than a relational one.

attributes.name: Scales
attributes.note: explicitly NOT a historical Raguel-specific attribute; a Didacus visual analogy for fairness and balance

attributes.name: Celestial motifs / star field
attributes.note: preserves the Enochic association with the luminaries

archangels.methodological_caution: This is the figure where the book must state most explicitly that the visual program is a contemporary reconstruction; 'harmony' and 'right relationship' are Didacus concepts, not quotations from 1 Enoch.
contemplative_prompts: Which relationship is out of balance?
Where is fairness required?
What would right relationship look like concretely?

archangels.name: Sariel / Saraqael
archangels.historical_role: Named as one of the holy angels in 1 Enoch 20 and assigned to spirits who sin in the spirit — connected with moral or spiritual transgression and oversight.

attributes.name: Scroll / book
attributes.note: iconographic record is sparse and heterogeneous; object vocabulary intentionally restrained

attributes.name: Star-tipped staff
attributes.note: no established visual type to draw on

attributes.name: Vigilant frontal gaze
attributes.note: reflects the Enochic assignment to spirits who sin

archangels.methodological_caution: Use the spelling Sariel (Saraqael/Saraqâêl) consistently and explain variant forms once; do not invent a medieval 'standard icon' where none can be established.
contemplative_prompts: What do I know but fail to discern?
Where do I rationalise what needs examination?
What does watchfulness look like without fear?

archangels.name: Remiel
name_variants: Jeremiel (later traditions — identity not fully stable across corpora)
archangels.historical_role: Seventh angel in 1 Enoch 20, assigned to 'those who rise,' commonly read in relation to resurrection. Later traditions use related names such as Jeremiel for figures associated with visions, souls, or eschatological reflection, but these identities should not be uncritically collapsed into one continuous personage.
primary_sources: later Jewish/Christian apocryphal traditions under related names

attributes.name: Open hand
attributes.note: emphasises hope as possibility rather than certainty

archangels.methodological_caution: Do not claim that 'Jeremiel' is simply another unproblematic spelling of Remiel across all sources; preserve the distinction between related names and traditions.
contemplative_prompts: What am I in the middle of leaving behind?
What do I hope for without certainty?
What threshold am I actually crossing?
